name: Quilt Film
character: A documentary on the wall: screenings and festivals first, the makers' stories behind them, and a producer's circle that finished the film.

sections.eyebrow: A documentary eight years in the making
sections.title: {{guild_name}}
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Three towns, nine quilters, and the quilts that held them together, filmed in kitchens and church basements across the state.

sections.heading: The film
sections.html:
The Long Thread follows nine quilt makers across three towns for eight years: a rodeo seamstress, a retired telephone operator, a father learning his late mother's patterns, and the guild hall that kept the lights on for all of them. It is a film about cloth that records time, and the people who keep recording it.

Shot on film because the subject deserved the same care, restored by the producer's circle when the lab closed, and finished in 2026 with the last fourteen reels paid for by members.

items.quote: The rare documentary that understands its subject is not the quilts. It is the hands.
items.author: A festival program note

items.quote: Our whole guild went on a bus. Half of us are in the film's credits under a thank-you that made us cry in the parking lot.
items.author: A Montana guild

sections.title: Screenings
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Theaters, guild halls, and one grange with legendary pie. Most screenings end with a talk-back and a quilt on display.

sections.heading: Host a screening
sections.html: Guilds, libraries, and small theaters can book the film with the community license: the projector specs, the discussion guide, and one of the quilts from the film, if the route allows it to travel. Write through the contact page and the calendar answers within the week.

sections.title: The long thread
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Eight years, ninety-one hours of footage, and three towns that adopted a camera crew.

sections.heading: How it was made
sections.html:
Shooting began as an archive project: record the guild's oldest members telling where their quilts came from. The archive became an obsession, the obsession became footage, and the footage became a film the length of a feature once the editors stopped being able to cut the women out.

Everything in the film is true, including the argument in the second act, which the participants have now seen twice and still disagree about, exactly as filmed.

sections.title: The producer's circle
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: The members who paid for the last reels, the restoration, and the bus routes to small towns.

sections.heading: Where the money went
sections.html: The circle bought the last fourteen reels of film when the lab closed, funded the frame-by-frame restoration, and underwrites the small-town screening routes where ticket sales never cover the projector bulb. The ledger is posted in the members' area, down to the film stock.

sections.title: The filmmakers
sections.subtitle: Sample text — replace me: Two documentarians who came for a weekend and stayed for eight years.

sections.html:
We came to record one guild's fortieth-anniversary quilt and stayed because the interview kept going after the tape technically stopped. Neither of us quilted when we arrived; both of us have opinionated stashes now, which we are told is the real graduation.

The film is independent, the circle is its only backer, and the crew list still fits on one page, which is how we intend to keep it.

items.quote: They filmed my mother's hands for two hours and used forty seconds. It is the forty seconds everyone talks about.
items.author: A film subject's daughter
